technical.lead: FMRB classified-annex deadline expires; eight-of-eight witness slate closes
technical.body: The Frontier Model Review Board executive order's ten-business-day classified-annex response clock reached T-zero on Friday May 22 itself, with the Friday morning intake window closing the witness slate at eight of eight on record as the NSA Director, the FBI Cyber Division Assistant Director, and the OMB Federal CIO all filed substantive responses against the Senate Cyber Subcommittee follow-up question set. A Friday Lawfare procedural note treated the eight-of-eight close inside the deadline window as the cleanest reading of the response curve the witness slate could have produced and the last open procedural gate at T-zero. A Friday Just Security analysis observed that White House OSTP has shifted its posture from the prior no-signing-window-before-May-22 line to a signing window open from end-of-day May 22 forward as the post-deadline session opened. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology held its Wednesday May 27 morning markup slot on the parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft and circulated a Friday-morning supplemental staff memorandum to committee members covering the now-closed Senate classified-annex record as the first formal House-track context document since the order's signing window opened.

technical.lead: n8n CVE day-22: exposed estate sub-900 as compliance-monitoring phase opens
technical.body: The Shadowserver day-twenty-two n8n CVE-2026-21858 (Ni8mare) Friday scan opened the first full post-deadline operating day with internet-exposed pre-1.121.0 instances continuing the descent to approximately 830 — the first sub-900 reading of the descent — and the residual long-tail unpatched share easing to about 6 percent as the federal-civilian compliance-monitoring window opened. The Friday scan report placed the US cohort easing to roughly 245 and the India cohort to approximately 130 as the federal-civilian remediation deadline transitioned into its compliance-monitoring phase. Censys honeypot telemetry reported exploitation attempts ticking down to approximately 1.3x baseline at the Friday 09:00 UTC mark — the first sub-1.5x weekday read in the descent and consistent with commodity-tier exploit-kit volume settling further into the post-deadline session as federal-civilian operators completed late-attestation submissions during the Friday morning window. CISA's Friday operations note confirmed the compliance-monitoring phase opening cleanly with the eleven-CVE Trail of Bits agent-loader taxonomy compliance window keyed to Friday May 22 now reaching T-zero and converting into a settled regulatory precedent, with the mandatory-attestation submission portal in its fourth full operating day total and first operating day inside the compliance-monitoring phase.

technical.lead: Mag-7 print cycle: Friday post-Alphabet tape lifts breakout cohort to 97 percent
technical.body: Alphabet's Thursday analyst-day script carried into Friday's pre-weekend tape as the canonical first post-event reaction session, with the desk preview cohort now treating Friday morning as the cleanest read on how the AI Services revenue-line breakout commitment prices into the Mag-7 follow-on print cycle ahead of the weekend close. A Friday 247 Wall St note reported the Bernstein, Wells Fargo Securities, Evercore ISI, Citi Research, Jefferies, and Goldman Sachs Equity Research preview cohort consensus stepping the Mag-7 breakout-cohort probability from Thursday's 96 percent to 97 percent — the highest reading the cohort has carried and the first reading inside one percentage point of unanimity — with the Friday cohort treating the now-published Alphabet analyst-day deck plus its updated investor-presentation footnotes as the canonical disclosure-precedent document set. A Friday VentureBeat aggregation reported the cohort confirming the Microsoft fiscal-Q3 print's expected disclosure-precedent commentary in the back half of June, with Meta and AWS following inside their fiscal-Q3 prints, and the cohort flagging that the post-event reaction session's pre-weekend tape provides the cleanest signal-to-noise read of the cycle since institutional-buyside positioning typically settles into the weekend hold ahead of Monday's continuation.

technical.lead: Cerebras Friday post-print: upper-band re-rating settles fourth session
technical.body: Cerebras CBRS carried Thursday's post-analyst-day re-rating into the Friday pre-weekend tape as the upper-half-of-analyst-band re-rating settled across a fourth consecutive trading session, with the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close advancing into the closing third of its late-Q2 2026 window and the cohort now reading the post-event reaction session as the canonical follow-on confirmation of Thursday's cross-program allocation read. A Friday BEAMSTART note reported the five-desk analyst spread tightening one notch further upward from Thursday's read — Bernstein's $185 Market-Perform floor still held, Morgan Stanley's $192 target with the upside-scenario probability stepping from Thursday's 51 percent to 54 percent inside its first full session above the half-probability threshold, Wells Fargo Securities Buy lifted from $215 to $220, Jefferies Outperform held at $225, and UBS Neutral lifted from $212 to $215 — with institutional-buyside cumulative net position lifting to roughly 44 percent of float as desks added incremental long exposure on the post-event reaction tape and the cohort flagging the cleared FMRB classified-annex eight-of-eight close as a second-order regulatory-anchor input compounding the cross-program allocation commentary.

technical.lead: Mistral Workflows day-22: Switzerland joins as 12th central-gov reference
technical.body: Mistral AI Workflows day-twenty-two Friday update lifted the sovereign-cloud central-government reference count to twelve, with Thursday's Norway Skatteetaten addition now joined by Switzerland's Federal Tax Administration as the first European Free Trade Association entrant to the cohort, and the cross-orchestrator interop matrix entering the final week before its first-week-of-June general-availability target. Mistral's Friday note reported the Swiss federal tax authority joining the prior eleven references — France DGFiP, Germany Bundesagentur fuer Arbeit, UK HMRC, Italy Agenzia delle Entrate, Spain AEAT, Portugal Autoridade Tributaria, Belgium FOD Financien, Netherlands Belastingdienst, Sweden Skatteverket, Denmark Skattestyrelsen, and Norway Skatteetaten — as the fifth fresh central-government estate selection of the business week; paid Workflows tenancy edged to approximately 431 enterprise customers and the daily-execution count to roughly 7.8M. Mistral confirmed that the six-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix holds its first-week-of-June general-availability target with the GA-readiness checklist clearing its final third entering the pre-GA week, shipping the six-surface mitigation set as a default with support for the sixteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter's tenant-policy field schemas.
